title: Serialization Security and Compatibility knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Trust boundaries for checkpoint files” in this lesson?
options: This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Record the artifact state and environment assumptions, restore it in a clean model, and verify behavior on a fixed input before trusting the result.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
questions.answer_key: Record the artifact state and environment assumptions, restore it in a clean model, and verify behavior on a fixed input before trusting the result.
questions.explanation: Trust boundaries for checkpoint files: Record the artifact state and environment assumptions, restore it in a clean model, and verify behavior on a fixed input before trusting the result.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Restricted loading options where supported”, what should a learner verify?
options: verify architecture compatibility, missing/unexpected keys, map location, and what state must be restored for inference versus resumed training.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
questions.answer_key: verify architecture compatibility, missing/unexpected keys, map location, and what state must be restored for inference versus resumed training.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: verify architecture compatibility, missing/unexpected keys, map location, and what state must be restored for inference versus resumed training.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Avoiding untrusted serialized objects”?
options: Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
Never load untrusted pickle-based checkpoint files; standard serialization can have security implications and compatibility limits.
questions.answer_key: Never load untrusted pickle-based checkpoint files; standard serialization can have security implications and compatibility limits.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Never load untrusted pickle-based checkpoint files; standard serialization can have security implications and compatibility limits.
